name: Negligence and breach of duty of care
description: Private-law constructs imposing liability when a person fails to meet a standard of care owed to others—one legal analogue (among others) to moral blame for culpable omission or sloth, though civil negligence does not require spiritual apathy.
foundationStrengthRationale: Common-law negligence and civilian analogues are well developed; standards of care remain fact-specific.

pros.claim: Translates avoidable carelessness into remediable harm without requiring criminal intent.
pros.evidence: Negligence dominates accident compensation in many jurisdictions.

cons.claim: Clinical depression, burnout, and structural overload undermine easy mapping from 'sloth' to legal breach.
cons.evidence: Disability and labor contexts show that non-performance often lacks moral blameworthiness.
